verses.text: If I could speak every human and angelic language but didn't have love, I'd be nothing but a loud gong or a crashing cymbal.
If I had the gift of prophecy and understood every mystery and all knowledge, and if I had enough faith to move mountains, but didn't have love, I would be nothing.
If I gave away everything I own to feed the poor, and even handed over my body to be burned, but didn't have love, I would gain nothing.
Love is patient and kind. It doesn't envy or brag, and it isn't arrogant.
It doesn't act rudely, insist on its own way, or get irritated. It doesn't keep a record of wrongs.
Love doesn't celebrate wrongdoing; it celebrates the truth.
It bears all things, trusts all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
Love never ends. Prophecies will pass away, languages will stop, and knowledge will pass away.
We know only part, and we prophesy only part.
But when completeness comes, what is partial will pass away.
When I was a child, I spoke, thought, and reasoned like a child. When I became an adult, I left childish ways behind.
For now we see only a dim reflection, but then we'll see face to face. Now I know only part, but then I'll know fully, just as God fully knows me.
For now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. And the greatest of these is love.
